source.title: Double descent is the principle of least action

record.tranche_reason: The study reports a model-size error curve using noisy polynomial regression rather than deep networks, a different method and model class from the original deep-network studies.
record.gate_note: The text describes its own polynomial-regression results in Figure 1, including a test-error curve and regularization-dependent function-discrepancy curves. Other double-descent results mentioned in the introduction are cited work, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly a theoretical account, but Figure 1E reports its own test-error curve over model size for noisy polynomial regression. It peaks at d = n and falls again beyond, which bears on V4 in a non-deep model class.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors argue, assuming ergodic equilibrated training, that finite training time acts as weight decay. They argue that equipartition cools the seen directions as d grows and that the interpolant's norm cannot increase with d. So going past interpolation acts as added weight-decay regularization. They state they have not directly shown this lowers test loss.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a noisy cubic regression task with Legendre-basis polynomials, least squares, and minimum-norm interpolation; it does not sweep deep-network widths or train deep networks.
record.method_sensitivity: The function-discrepancy peak varies with the weight-decay value; the text relates each curve's peak to where σmin(A)² falls below λ.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 2 proves that the norm of the minimum-norm interpolant is nonincreasing in d for d ≥ n. Theorem 1 shows that finite training time acts like weight decay λ + 1/t. The authors interpret going past interpolation as added effective weight-decay regularization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterization beyond the interpolation threshold acts as implicit L2 regularization, lowering the solution norm as d grows.

fits_no_version.finding: The figure caption says label-noise amplification into the fit is governed by 1/(σmin(A)² + λ), with σmin(A)² collapsing at d = n (Fig. 1G). This is a derivation and illustration, not a measured test of V6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The double-descent peak arises from ill-conditioning of the fitting matrix at d = n amplifying label noise, damped by weight decay.

record.problems: The reported numerical results are in figures without values stated in the text. The main test-error result is one polynomial-regression setup with n = 20, and the authors say they have not directly shown that the proposed effects decrease test loss.

untested.parts: No deep networks are trained; the only experiment is polynomial regression.
No sweep of test error over training epochs.
Sample size is fixed at n = 20.
Only one model class (Legendre polynomial regression) and one dataset; other model classes are not tested.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epochs and samples.
Label noise level is not varied. Multiple peaks and peak removal by optimally tuned regularization are not tested.
There is no recount of effective parameters and no test of whether the curve becomes U-shaped.

record.verdict_notes: This is largely a theory and pedagogy paper. Its only empirical content is the illustrative polynomial experiment in Fig. 1, reported as figures without numbers. The record's V6 limits_scope label rested on untested parts, which is not a valid basis, so it is dropped. The paper is not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses polynomial regression, not deep networks.
No test-error sweep over training epochs is reported.
The number of training samples is not varied to test whether more data raises test error.
The reported test is limited to one polynomial-regression setup; other model classes are not tested.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested for predicting peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study does not test multiple or split peaks, or whether an optimally tuned regularizer eliminates the test-error peak.
The study does not recount complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether that makes the curve an ordinary U-shape.

conditions.value: noisy samples of a cubic; ξᵢ ∼ N(0, 0.4²)
d varied across the plotted sweep; interpolation threshold d = n

rows.note: The text describes a classical U-shape initially, a peak at d = n, and a long decreasing tail to the right; the plotted values are not given numerically.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. The value is figure-only. The setup reproduces the Nakkiran et al. toy example (n = 20 noisy cubic samples), shown as one illustrative run with no seeds or uncertainty.

rows.subject: Legendre-basis polynomial regression
rows.operation_detail: Compare the function discrepancy across model sizes under four weight-decay values.

conditions.value: noisy samples of a cubic; ξᵢ ∼ N(0, 0.4²)
four values; individual values not stated in the text

rows.measure: Root mean square distance from the true cubic over I = [x₁, xₙ]
rows.locator: Figure 1F and its caption; discussion of Figure 1G
rows.note: The text says each curve peaks where σmin(A)² falls below its λ and describes amplification of label noise into the fit as governed by 1/(σmin(A)² + λ). This is a function-discrepancy measure, not the test-error measure in Figure 1E.
rows.check: The record's 'observed' is not supported. The text says only that each of the λ curves still peaks where σmin(A)² falls below λ. It gives no values and does not say whether peak height shrinks or any λ removes the peak. The measure is distance to the true cubic over the training-input range, a test-error proxy. It cannot show V6's claimed disappearance under optimal tuning.

relationships.condition: Legendre-basis polynomial regression, n = 20 noisy cubic samples, least squares for d ≤ n, minimum-norm interpolant for d > n
relationships.reason: The test error is U-shaped at first, peaks at d = n, then decreases in a long tail (r1, Fig. 1E, figure only).
relationships.display_finding: Test error was initially U-shaped, peaked at d = n = 20, and then decreased along a long tail.
